neighbours.label: an adjective or noun opening a careful examination ('a careful analysis of', 'a close inspection of', 'a cursory glance')
fire: It is clear from a careful reading of the contract.
But a close examination of the accounts says otherwise.
It opens with a detailed review of the data.
Moreover, a cursory look at the budget confirms it.
This follows from a careful study of the map.
Yet a closer inspection of the wall shows cracks.
The paper rests on a thorough analysis of the survey.
Even a quick glance at the chart reveals the gap.
quiet: It is clear from a large copy of the contract.
But a young member of the staff says otherwise.
It opens with a loud burst of the song.
Moreover, a round table at the back confirms it.
This follows from a heavy fall of the snow.
Yet a darker shade of the wall shows cracks.
The paper rests on a small pile of the books.
Even a blue line on the chart reveals the gap.

notes: ' close' in 'a close friend' read 0.35 in a probe, so the word alone leaks; none of the near misses use it.
